chunks: And from him, from Muhammad ibn 'Ubayd ibn 'Utbah, from al-Kufi, from al-Fadl ibn Dukayn Abu Nu'aym, who said: Abd al-Salam ibn Harb narrated to us from Ayyub al-Sijistani, from Abu Qilabah, from Abu Hurayrah, who said:
The Messenger of Allah (peace be upon him and his family) said: 'The month of Ramadan has come to you, a blessed month, a month in which Allah has made fasting obligatory for you.'
In it, the gates of Paradise are opened, and the devils are chained.
'The Night of Decree is better than a thousand months.'
Whoever is deprived of it has been deprived [of all good].
ai.seo_question: What are the virtues and rulings of the month of Ramadan according to this hadith?
ai.summary: Recorded in Shaykh al-Tusi’s *Tahdhib al-Ahkam* within the chapter on the obligation of fasting, this hadith serves as a foundational prophetic declaration marking the commencement of Ramadan. It emphasizes the cosmic significance of the month by linking the physical act of fasting with spiritual liberation—specifically the opening of Paradise’s gates and the chaining of devils—while elevating Laylat al-Qadr as the pinnacle of worship, surpassing a thousand months in reward.
